summary: Flags 'else' blocks following an 'if' containing a breaking statement (return, break, continue, throw), as they are unreachable.
firingShapes: try { if (i) { throw new Error(); } else { j(); } } catch {}
function f() { if (k) { return 1; } else { return 2; } }
switch(s) { case 1: if (m) { break; } else { n++; } default: break; }
label: if (o) { break label; } else { p(); }
if (q) { return r(); } else { s = t; }
silentShapes: if (x) { y = z; } else { if (a) { b(); } }
function f() { if (c) { d(); } else { return; } }
if (e) { try { f(); } finally { g(); } } else { h(); }
do { if (i) { break; } else { j++; } } while (k);
fixDescription: Removes the 'else' block and places its statements directly after the 'if' block at the same indentation level.
hazards: Moving a 'var' declaration from the else block to outer scope changes its function-scoped visibility and may cause hoisting conflicts.
If the else block contains a labeled break/continue targeting an outer loop, removing the else block may break the label reference or alter control flow.
Comments attached to the 'else' keyword or its braces may be lost or misplaced during the rewrite.
If the else block declares a function, moving it outer may change its hoisting timing relative to other declarations.
When the if block contains 'continue', the else block's removal may affect loop iteration counts if the else had side effects before the continue.
In a switch case, removing the else block may fall through unintentionally if the original else was preventing fall-through via a break.
If the else block contains a 'with' statement, moving it outer changes the scope chain for its enclosed statements.
An else block returning a value via an arrow function may rely on lexical 'this' from its original block scope, which could differ when moved.
If the else block is empty, the fix removes unnecessary braces but may remove a deliberate code placeholder or comment.
When the if block throws, the else block's removal is safe only if no subsequent code depends on the exception being caught elsewhere.
